{"code": "import re

# Re-examine the revenue column to find all values with commas
# Look for any value containing a comma
revenue_with_comma = df['revenue'].str.contains(',', na=False)

print(f"Number of revenue values with commas: {revenue_with_comma.sum()}")
print(f"Values with commas: {df['revenue'][revenue_with_comma].unique()}")

# The only value with a comma is '999,999.99', which appears 6 times (as per documentation)
qa_mask = df['revenue'] == '999,999.99'
print(f"Number of rows with '999,999.99': {qa_mask.sum()}")

# These are the QA orders — they should be excluded from revenue calculation
# Remove them from the dataset
df_clean = df[~qa_mask]

# Also remove refunded orders
refunded_mask = df_clean['status'] == 'refunded'
print(f"Number of refunded orders after removing QA: {refunded_mask.sum()}")

# Filter out refunded orders
df_final = df_clean[~refunded_mask]

# Now convert revenue to float after removing commas
# Strip commas and convert to float
revenue_clean = df_final['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False)
revenue_clean = pd.to_numeric(revenue_clean, errors='coerce')

# Fill any NaN with 0.00 (though there shouldn't be any)
revenue_clean = revenue_clean.fillna(0.00)

# Assign to DataFrame
df_final['revenue_clean'] = revenue_clean

# Compute total revenue by channel
revenue_by_channel = df_final.groupby('channel')['revenue_clean'].sum()

# Find the channel with the highest total revenue
max_channel = revenue_by_channel.idxmax()
max_revenue = revenue_by_channel.max()

print("Final total revenue by channel:")
print(revenue_by_channel)
print(f"Channel with highest revenue: {max_channel} with {max_revenue:.2f}")"}
